parsed.summary: Lean proves three things about R_k(3). First, R_k(3)^{1/k} → ∞. Second, an explicit lower bound R_k(3) ≥ ((1/(6e^{38})) k^{1/3}/log k)^k holds for all k ≥ 2. Third, log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k). The most important caveat: the theorem `triangleRamseyNumber_log_sharp_coefficients` is stated as `∃ ε, 0 < ε → …`, which is vacuously true (take ε = 0), so the sharp k^{(1/3−o(1))k} ≤ R_k(3) ≤ k^{(1+o(1))k} bounds are not actually formalized.

glossary.plain: A k-edge-colouring C of K_n has no monochromatic triangle: each colour class graph is K_3-free.
Every k-colouring of E(K_n) contains a monochromatic triangle.
glossary.note: For k = 0 and n ≥ 2 no labelings exist, so the condition holds vacuously. This is only a small-k edge case.

glossary.plain: R_k(3) = least n such that every k-colouring of E(K_n) has a monochromatic triangle (sInf; would be 0 if the set were empty).
glossary.note: For k ≥ 1 the set is nonempty by Ramsey's theorem, so the sInf junk value is not hit. For k = 0 the value is 2 rather than any conventional value; this is irrelevant asymptotically and for k ≥ 2.

lean_claims.plain: There exists a real ε such that, IF ε > 0, then eventually (1/3−ε) k log k ≤ log R_k(3) ≤ (1+ε) k log k. This is trivially true by choosing ε ≤ 0.
log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k) as k → ∞ (both big-O directions).

paper_claims.plain: There is an absolute c > 0 with R_k(3) ≥ (c k^{1/3}/log k)^k for all integers k ≥ 2.

coverage.why: Lean gives an explicit constant c = 1/(6e^{38}) for all k ≥ 2.
log R_k = Θ(k log k) is the same as R_k = k^{Θ(k)}.
The quantifier `∃ ε, 0 < ε → …` makes the statement vacuous.

flags.explanation: The statement is `∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → …`. Taking ε = 0 makes the hypothesis false, so the theorem is trivially true and says nothing. The intended statement is `∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ k in atTop, …`, i.e. the 1/3 − o(1) and 1 + o(1) exponents. As written, the sharp coefficients are not formalized at all.
flags.probe_idea: Prove `∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → False` via ⟨0, lt_irrefl 0⟩ to show vacuity. Restate as `∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, ((1/3:ℝ) - ε) * k * Real.log k ≤ Real.log (triangleRamseyNumber k) ∧ Real.log (triangleRamseyNumber k) ≤ (1 + ε) * k * Real.log k`.

flags.explanation: For k = 0, labelings of K_n with n ≥ 2 do not exist, so the defined value is 2. This is a harmless edge case, since every claim is either asymptotic or restricted to k ≥ 2.
The explicit constant 1/(6e^{38}) is stronger than the paper's existential c. This is fine.
